questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: which courses to choose at the destination and also the environment was very important for me. Therefore Svalbard was the perfect on for me. I love the Arctic environment and find it very fascinating. The learning environment is so good, some of the best teachers I have ever had.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I can recommend everyone I know to take on exchange, it is so giving!! I would love to do it again.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: All the information was given before I left, so it was very easy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didn't need anything

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: When you study at UNIS on Svalbard, you search for housing at Samskipnaden and you will get a room. It is the only place you can live on Svalbard as a student. It is a student house

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: It is a student house. So there is a big kitchen for 6-10 people, and all the basic stuff is in the kitchen and if you need anything, you can write to the people, and maybe you will get it.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is an amazing place to live! I would highly recommend it

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You need to your documents in time other than that it is pretty simple and they write a lot of emails on where to find what

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could always write them an email if necessary and you will get a respond quickly

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: 100 %, there is also only one semester course in Biology so I got that one and it was good

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Remember to send in your documents in time, that is the key word.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses was really inspiring. I learned so much in just in one semester. The level of courses was good. It can be hard to teach people from different background, but they did a really good job

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very different. At my host institution were we 18 people in my class and that was it. So they teaching style was like going in primary school again in a good way. At my host institution they broad in the expert to teach on subjects, so we had one teacher in 3 days, then a new teacher came in and were there 4 days and so on. I like it was in that way. We learned very different teaching ways and found some quite inspiring and fascinated people on my way!

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Arctic Population Ecology 
Terrestrial Arctic Biology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Both! It two really good courses if you are interested in the Arctic environment

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: If you travel to an Arctic environment, you should be prepare to spend some money on warm cloth such as merino wool and a shell jacket. In an Arctic environment you will put on cloth layer on layer and that costs money

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Less expensive was that you don't buy books, you got all the material by your host university. 
More expensive was cloth and food because you are in the Arctic

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was a friday gathering were all the students could show up and get a beer of soda and hang out in the cafeteria. It you had a great idea anything could happen! Some also had a jiu jitsu class where people could show up.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Friday gathering was a really good idea! then you could also meet other students 
If you have a great idea, then just ask around and it will properly happen

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on hikes !! it is the most beautiful place in the whole world! Visit a café and sit a knit

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: The local community is the sweetest people! They are so friendly and open. So I will say pretty easy, just be open. Everyone speaks english

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: There is no local students, but some have been there one semester before. Just talk to the people you meet and be open. Say yes to thing, even though it's not you. Try new thing

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I didn't

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That they were friendly and open.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Join in "Bruktikken", it is a thrift shop where everything is free. amazing!
Be open, say yes to new things 
Go on hikes if the weather is good! appreciate when the sun is there and there is no clouds, go out!!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Take on an exchange if you want to

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people, the teaching and personal development

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I have not always loved english... But on an exchange you a forced to speak english to be with people. So for me was it definitely the english.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
